newsitem.title: ROMANIA: FRANCE TELECOM LAUNCHES ROMANIA SECOND GSM SYSTEM.
newsitem.headline: FRANCE TELECOM LAUNCHES ROMANIA SECOND GSM SYSTEM.

text.p: A consortium led by France Telecom on Friday launched Romania's second GSM mobile phone system with hopes to attract some 700,000 subscribers over the next 10 years.

Andrei Chirica, General Manager of the Mobil Rom consortium, told reporters the Dialog GSM service -- a brand name chosen by the Mobifon consortium to run the project -- would cover all cities with a population of over 100,000 and the main national roads and airports by end-1997.
"We plan to invest $500 million to roll out and develop this GSM project," Chirica said.
Last November, Mobil Rom won one of the two 10-year licences offered in a tender by the Communications Ministry. France Telecom owns 51% of Mobil Rom.

The other winner was the Mobifon consortium led by Canada's Telesystem International Wireless. Mobifon launched Romania's first GSM operation in April with the ambitious target to get over one million subscribers in 10 years.
Chirica said some 8,000 people had already signed up to Dialog ahead of the official launch ceremony on Friday.
The system is now operational in eight major cities and on the roads connecting them, Chirica said.
He said Mobil Rom was planning a fast roll-out of the project and cover with the new digital system Romania's main cities and European transit routes within the next 12 months.
"We will cover all towns with over 20,000 inhabitants and all national roads, which means that 89 percent of Romania's population will have access to the system," he said.

Local media said GSM had become very popular since Mobifon launched the first system in the Balkan country, where only 3.1 million of its 23 million people subscribe to the fixed network. Penetration rate is only 13 percent, one of the lowest in Europe.
A Mobifon official refused on Friday to elaborate on the number of its subscribers.
Ex-communist Romania is the last state in the region to set up a digital GSM system. The licence has a frequency concession tax amounting to $50 million.
The Mobil Rom consortium includes local companies Media Pro and Computer Land as well as investors Tomen Telecom Romania and Alcatel Network Systems Romania.
